main_text.p: Hoc, Hermanne, notant virides (me iudice) rana Succineo clausa tumulo, non funera Regum. Non ea laus ranis, nec gratia tanta lacertis. Rana Sophistarum mendacia garrula, rana Exprimit ingenium morésque libidine foedos. Vix alio poterat natura animante Suitas Pingere commodius, Romanaque monstra notare.
main_text.head: DIPNOSOPHISTA.
main_text.p: HOc quoque, Sofiade, praeter narrata petenti Respode:numerare inter quibus artibus acres Theologos possim, quos horrent cuncta tremuntque, Suspiciuntque omnes, praesensque ut Numen adorant: Quos aula Procerum ditant, quos curia Patrum, Quos admiratur plebs infima, miles, equesque? Audi igitur, dabimus praecepta brevissima queis [?]si Parveris, non est quisquam ut te vincere possit, Seu Cameriaden superet, sive arte Philippum. Principio, Rudis esse stude. Si forte pudoris Fronte quid est residens, abrade: audaculus esto, Scurra, liguritor, vinosus, avarus, amator, Litis amans, quosuis promptus damnare, superbus, Livldus, & mordax convitia fundere folers, Inprimis in eos, quos infamare solemus Nomine Calvini[?]: deque ist is quidlibet aude.

page.notes: The large initial H of "HOc" is a woodcut-style initial, joined to its word. Several words are uncertain from the scan: "Respode:numerare" (colon as printed), "queis si" (line end blurred, marked [?]), "Calvini" (smudged, marked [?]). The second poem's line "Livldus" is as printed in the scan, possibly for "Lividus". The first poem's lines are run together because the scan shows no stanza breaks. The printed line-ends were not kept as line breaks, per the paragraph rule for verse blocks.
